ledger.claim: POL-NS-01(c) makes the fee chargeable only if the driver 'held position inside' the arrival geofence for a continuous dwell of at least 300 seconds for this LARGE_VENUE pickup. The record never shows a 300-second continuous hold. The driver's two qualifying holds are 170 seconds (18:44:45 to 18:47:35) and 185 seconds (18:49:35 to 18:52:40), separated by a 120-second excursion in which he left the 120 m arrival radius and reached 179.0 m from the pin. The longest continuous run is 185 seconds, 115 seconds short of the minimum, so limb (c) fails and the fee is not chargeable.

The only route to 300 seconds is to add the two short holds together under POL-NS-06(i), and that limb applies only where the advisory made 'holding position ... not lawfully possible'. The trace shows the driver holding the very kerbside bay the advisory is said to cover continuously for 185 seconds, and his own message at 18:47:50 records a self-chosen loop ('i go one round and come back', MSG-00214-004), not an enforced removal; the premise of the exception is not made out. In any event POL-NS-06(i) is a qualification on the POL-NS-06 refund computation and does not enlarge the continuous-dwell condition in POL-NS-01(c); the exception must be construed strictly and cannot convert two sub-minimum holds into the continuous 300-second dwell the clause demands.

The driver cannot answer the shortfall with the rider's whereabouts. POL-NS-06 makes the dwell test decisive 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages', and the chat log shows the rider did respond and coordinate ('ok coming down now', MSG-00214-003, 18:46:20). On the raw trace the effective continuous dwell is 185 seconds against a 300-second minimum, so POL-NS-06 directs a full refund of the SGD 4.00 and no driver compensation is payable.

If the applicability of POL-NS-06(i) is genuinely open on this record, the fact that decides the charge is unresolved and the case falls to be escalated under POL-NS-09 rather than decided by the automated pipeline. Escalation is terminal and, unlike a ruling on the merits, leaves the disputed SGD 4.00 held rather than collected or refunded, so the rider is not left carrying the charge while the question — whether a kerb restriction that the trace shows him holding for 185 continuous seconds really made holding 'not lawfully possible' — is settled by a human reviewer.

The arrival test is satisfied on the driver's own trace: 40 qualifying in-geofence fixes fall within the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, the first of them at 18:44:45, and the trip_record carries an 'arrived' event at 18:44:30 with the pickup pinned at ION Orchard's registered PHV bay. POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) therefore hold, and POL-NS-02's proximity test is passed rather than failed.

The effective dwell exceeds the minimum. The trace shows two stationary holds — 170 seconds running from 18:44:45 and 185 seconds running from 18:49:35 — separated by a single loop during which the driver never went further than 179.0 m from the pin, comfortably inside the 300 m leash. EV-ADVIS-00214-01 is a populated LTA KERB_RESTRICTION whose geometry covers the pickup road and whose 17:00-20:00 window covers the whole waiting period, so holding position was not lawfully possible and POL-NS-06(i) permits the two in-geofence intervals to be summed. Accumulated dwell is 355 seconds against the 300 second LARGE_VENUE minimum — a surplus of 55 seconds, not a shortfall.

Termination satisfies POL-NS-01 limb (d): the driver cancelled at 18:52:45 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, five seconds after the second hold ended at 18:52:40 — that is, at or after the moment the accumulated dwell requirement elapsed. No boarding event is recorded anywhere in the trip record, so the trip was correctly terminated by the driver on a no-show basis rather than the driver admitting he could not locate the rider.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider on this record. Limb (b) fails first: the rider wrote 'ok coming down now' at 18:46:20 and the driver replied at 18:47:50, 90 seconds later — inside the 120 second window — and at any rate the rider's 18:46:20 message is a status statement, not a locating message giving an entrance, block, tower or bay. Limb (c) is also affirmatively failed: the rider's device never came closer than 690.7 m to the pickup pin against the 150 m LARGE_VENUE presence radius, and there are zero rider qualifying fixes.

There is no false arrival marker under POL-NS-05. At the 18:44:30 marker the driver's track shows stationary speeds — 0.0 kph appears among the distinct speeds — and the first qualifying in-geofence fix follows only 15 seconds later at 18:44:45. The marker is neither more than 300 m from the pin nor taken while travelling at 15 km/h or above, so the waiting clock runs from the arrival event and nothing is recomputed against the driver.

No wrong-entrance case arises under POL-NS-03 and no pin-ambiguity goodwill is owed to anyone. The pickup zone has a single registered pickup point, so POL-NS-03(ii)'s two-or-more-points precondition is absent, and the driver's stationary fixes fall inside the 120 m arrival radius — so the clause's premise, a driver stationary outside that radius but within 400 m, is simply not met.

The chat log corroborates the driver rather than the rider's account of a car wandering about. At 18:45:10 the driver gave the exact bay and vehicle ('im at the ION PHV bay along Orchard Turn, white Vios'); at 18:47:50, on the marshal's instruction, he told the rider in terms that he was going one round and returning to the same place — which matches the trace's single 18:47:35-18:49:35 loop and his prompt return to the same kerb. That is a driver managing a kerbside restriction, not a driver abandoning the pickup.

The $4.00 charged is exactly what fee_schedule.resolution_rule produces: the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00), which agree here. The fare_breakdown cancellation_fee reconciles with that figure, so the fare line is not defective and POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged.

Compensation is payable to the driver under POL-NS-07 because POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the threshold of 4, and measured against driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 118 the ratio is 0.017, far below 0.08. The driver is therefore owed 80 percent of the fee — SGD 3.20 — with the fee itself standing.

No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is present. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the abuse threshold of 3; rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so there is no repeat-pair pattern; and every artifact in the bundle is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no issue codes fired, so no deciding fact rests on impaired evidence and no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The SGD 4.00 no-show cancellation fee stands and the driver is paid SGD 3.20, being 80% of that fee under POL-NS-07. The ruling value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION and the figure 3.20 sits in both money fields because POL-GEN-03 requires it on a driver-compensation ruling; it is the amount this ruling moves, not a second payment and not a refund to the rider, whose charge stands.

The fee. The trip record shows the driver arrived at the ION Orchard PHV bay at 18:44:30 and cancelled at 18:52:45 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. The GPS trace is complete (100% coverage, no gaps, weight 1.0) and contains 40 qualifying in-radius fixes inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, so POL-NS-02 is satisfied and POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) hold. Limb (d) holds: the driver terminated the trip on a no-show code at 18:52:45, with no boarding event recorded anywhere.

The dwell, which is the point the rider argues. The rider is right about the raw arithmetic: no single continuous hold reaches 300 seconds. The two holds are 170 s (18:44:45 to 18:47:35) and 185 s (18:49:35 to 18:52:40), and the longest is 185 s. But POL-NS-06(i) is the rule this policy gives for how that dwell limb is measured where a kerb restriction is in force: it permits separate in-geofence intervals within one pickup attempt to be summed, provided the driver never went more than 300 m from the pin and a qualifying advisory covered the road and the waiting window. Both conditions are met. The driver's furthest point during the 18:47:35 to 18:49:35 loop was 179.0 m, inside the 300 m leash, and EV-ADVIS-00214-01 is a populated LTA KERB_RESTRICTION (full-day bus lane, no stopping, waiting or picking up, 17:00 to 20:00 on Orchard Turn) whose geometry covers the pickup road and whose active window covers the whole waiting period. The rider's contrary argument, that the exception cannot apply because the driver was able to hold the kerb for 185 s and that POL-NS-06(i) cannot enlarge the word 'continuous' in POL-NS-01(c), is rejected: POL-NS-06(i) is precisely the provision that states whether separate stretches are summed, and the advisory's own terms (vehicles holding the kerb will be moved on) together with the driver's 18:47:50 message that the marshal moved him on show that holding position was not lawfully possible. Accumulated dwell is 355 seconds against the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum, a surplus of 55 seconds, so POL-NS-06 does not displace the charge.

Other clauses. POL-NS-03 is not engaged: the zone has one registered pickup point, so the pin-ambiguity precondition is absent, and the driver's stationary fixes are inside the arrival radius rather than outside it. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider: the driver replied at 18:47:50, 90 seconds after the rider's 18:46:20 message, inside the 120-second window, and limb (c) is affirmatively failed because the rider's device never came closer than about 690 m to the pin (zero qualifying rider fixes) against the 150 m LARGE_VENUE presence radius. POL-NS-05 is not engaged: at the 18:44:30 marker the driver was not more than 300 m from the pin and not travelling at 15 km/h or above, so the marker is not false and the waiting clock is not recomputed against him. POL-NS-08 is not engaged: the 4.00 fee equals the greater of the 4.00 LARGE_VENUE zone fee and the 4.00 RYDE_X tier fee, and every artifact in the bundle is COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

Driver compensation and escalation. POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, so POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the 4.00 fee, 3.20, with the residual 0.80 retained as the platform service fee. The anti-farming check does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 2 (below 4) and 2 of 118 completed trips is 0.017 (below 0.08). No POL-NS-09 trigger fires: confidence is above the 0.70 floor; rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so there is no repeat-pair pattern; rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below 3; no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; and no deciding fact rests on impaired evidence. The rider's request for escalation is therefore refused, because the applicability of POL-NS-06(i) is not genuinely open on this record. No referral fires: POL-NS-05(ii) has no application because the arrival marker is not false.

Confidence. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact, the GPS trace, the trip record, the traffic advisory, the fare breakdown and the driver profile, carries weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and confidence is set at 0.90. No context-only profile field (rating, account_age_days, lifetime_trips, cancellation_rate, prior_no_show_flags and the like) was used as a ground of decision.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
